               <ns0:p n="8">8 And many nations shall pass by this city, and they shall say every man to his neighbour, wherefore hath the LORD done thus to this great city <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">According to Gods threatnings, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 29.24. 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 9.8. though the Jews would not understand that there was a cause, yet others would understand it, and inquire into it.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Then they shall answer, Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their GOD <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Some shall answer them, or they shall answer one another. Surely it is because they have broken the divine Law, which the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> made a Covenant, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 19.8. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 24.3.7. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 5.27. upon which account their sinning was an Aposta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy and a <ns0:hi>forsaking their Covenant.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and worshipped other gods, and served them <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Their sinning was not of an ordinary nature, but by Idolatry, worshipping Images, and Idols which indeed were no Gods, but only in the opinion of those nations that worshipped them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 ¶ Weep ye not for the dead, neither be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moan him <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Not for <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> your dead Prince, for whom there was a great mourning, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 35.25. mentioned, <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 12.11. <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> is happy, you need not trouble your selves for him, but weep for <ns0:hi>Iehoa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> who is to go, or is gone into Captivity, <ns0:hi>Ieho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> was set up upon his fathers death by the people, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 23.30. 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.1. but verse 3. put down within three moneths and carried into <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> verse 4. where he died, 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 23.34.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> weep sore for him that goeth away <ns0:hi>s</ns0:hi>; for he shall return no more, nor see his native country <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">So as he no more returned into <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> the participle be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing in the present tense inclineth me to think, that this prophesie, was long before that in the former chapter, soon after the death of <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> upon the peoples setting up of <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>oa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> in his stead, or presently after he was carried away. Some interpret this of the people that were dead, and those that were going into Captivity, but the next verse makes it far more probable that it is to be understood of <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">For thus saith the LORD touching Shallum, the son of Josiah king of Judah <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Who this <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> was is a little doubted, some think it was <ns0:hi>Iehoa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> the Son of <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. called <ns0:hi>Iohanan,</ns0:hi> there is also mentioned one <ns0:hi>Shallum,</ns0:hi> but he is there mentioned as the fourth son of <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> in the Book of <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> we read only of three Sons which <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> had, <ns0:hi>viz. Iehoa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az, Iehojachim,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dekiah,</ns0:hi> most think that this <ns0:hi>Shallum,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Iehoa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>az</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iohanan</ns0:hi> (as he is called 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15.) who was indeed the second son of <ns0:hi>Iosiah</ns0:hi> for it is plain from 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 23.31, 36. that <ns0:hi>Iehoja<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chim</ns0:hi> was two years older, otherwise he could not have been 25 years old when he began to reign after <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> who began to reign at 23 years of age and reigned but three months, but 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. he is called <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> first-born, because he was first made King, and here he is called <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> for the shortness of his reign, in derision to the Jews who so called him, upon the account of their good hopes of prosperity under him, and in allusion to <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> the son of <ns0:hi>Iabesh,</ns0:hi> one of the last Kings of the ten Tribes mentioned 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 15.13. who reigned but a moneth, for this as some think could not be that <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned after <ns0:hi>Zedekiah,</ns0:hi> as the fourth son of <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.15. for that <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> they say never reigned, this as the text saith did reign three months</ns0:note>, which reigned in stead of Josiah his father <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>instead of Iosiah his Father,</ns0:hi> which phrase seemeth also to conclude that he immediately succeeded his Father <ns0:hi>Iosiah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, which went forth out of this place <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He was carried away from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> presently after he was set up, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 23.31, 32. imprisoned at <ns0:hi>Ribla<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> and verse 34. died in <ns0:hi>Egypt.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, he shall not return thither any more.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But he shall dye in the place whither they have led him captive, and shall see this land no more <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">So as he returned no more to see his native Country, as is here said. But others think this <ns0:hi>Shallum</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> fourth son, that <ns0:hi>Iohanan</ns0:hi> died before his father, and the people made <ns0:hi>Shal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lum</ns0:hi> his youngest Son <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> calling him <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz,</ns0:hi> so as he reign<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed immediately after <ns0:hi>Iosiah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ Wo unto him that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mich. 3.10. Hab. 2.9.</ns0:note> buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by wrong<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                  <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">We have not here any certain guidance to let us know whether the Prophet intended <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iehojachim,</ns0:hi> both of them <ns0:hi>did evil in the sight of the Lord</ns0:hi> as we read in their story, the sin here reflected upon is manifestly <ns0:hi>injustice</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>oppression,</ns0:hi> but possibly in the former part of the verse, all injust, and oppres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sive acts, by which either of these Princes endeavoured to pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mote their grandeur may be understood, for we need not take, <ns0:hi>building his house</ns0:hi> in a strict literal sense, but signifying the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />motion of his Family or establishing his State and Dignity.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> useth his neighbours service without wages, and giveth him not for his work <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">In the latter part a special oppression, withholding workmens wages, is the sin upon which the wo is denounced, a sin contra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry to the Law, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 19.13. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 24.14, 15. and against which the judgment of God is also denounced under the New Testament, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 5.4. An evident demonstration of Gods love to mankind securing by his Law, just dealings between man and man, and revenging acts of injustice, and particularly where men take advantage of their greatness above, and superiority over others, to trample them under their feet, and to with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold their rights from them, though such persons may be out of the reach of humane justice, yet God hath denounced a wo against them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 That saith, I will build me a wide house, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>through aired.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> large chambers, and cutteth him out <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>my wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dowes.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> windows, and <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> cieled with cedar, and painted with vermilion <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">That is wo to that man, who suffering oppression in his Government, or making it his business himself to oppress, yet buildeth himself, great houses and large chambers cieling them with Cedar, promising himself prosperity and splendor not<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />withstanding his wicked courses; for otherwise it is lawful enough for Princes to build themselves stately houses, &c. yet some think, that <ns0:hi>Iehojachims</ns0:hi> Pride, and <ns0:hi>Luxury</ns0:hi> and magnifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cence is here blamed, which also may be, considering what fate he was under, for <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> was reprieved only during <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> life, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 34.24, 25, 26, 27, 28. and this Prince had seen, <ns0:hi>Shal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lum</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iehoahaz</ns0:hi> his Brother carried into Captivity, and he still walked in the same wicked courses his brother had done, yet in contempt of the Word of the Lord by <ns0:hi>Huldah</ns0:hi> in his Fathers time, he promiseth himself all prosperity, and splendor, and accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ingly was building himself stately Houses, and adorning them, for this the woe is here denounced.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">Shalt thou reign because thou closest <ns0:hi>thy self</ns0:hi> in Cedar <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Art thou so vain as to think that brave Houses will continue thy Kingdom? Thou art mistaken, magnificent buildings are not those things which establish a Princes Throne.</ns0:note>? did not thy father eat and drink, and do judgment and justice, and then <ns0:hi>it was</ns0:hi> well with him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">How was it with thy Father? He lived prosperously yet had no such state<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Edifices, his Throne was established by Justice, and Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, that were the right way for thee to sit sure upon thy Throne.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 He judged the cause of the poor and needy <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">By himself in person for the Kings of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten sate personally to judge causes: or by setting such Judges as did it, administring justice impartially, particularly to such as in respect of their low condition were most exposed to the pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er of others, and doing thus he prospered.</ns0:note>, then <ns0:hi>it was</ns0:hi> well <ns0:hi>with him: was</ns0:hi> not this to know me? saith the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This was for him truly to own and acknowledge me, they onely truly know God who obey him, and men vainly pretend to Piety, who are noto<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />riously defective in duties of Justice and Charity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 But thine eyes and thy heart <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> not but for thy covetousness <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">All that thou lookest after, and that thy heart is set upon, is thy own <ns0:hi>grandeur,</ns0:hi> and riches.</ns0:note>, and for to shed innocent blood, and for oppression, and for <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> violence to do <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And to make thy self great thou makest no difficulty, to destroy thy subjects that are inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cent, and have not deserved death, and to oppress others, using all manner of violence against them, it is not to be thought that <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> did all this in person; but by such corrupt and injust Judges, as he set up; so God accounted that <ns0:hi>Ahab</ns0:hi> had <ns0:hi>killed,</ns0:hi> and taken <ns0:hi>possession,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 21.19. Though the <ns0:hi>Elders and Nobles</ns0:hi> were those that did it, <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> 11.12, 13. Princes are responsal to God for the sins of their Ministers and Judges.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:31" />18 Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning Jehojakim the son of Josiah king of Judah <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">A very bad son of a good Father whose name was <ns0:hi>Eliakim,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Pharaoh Necho</ns0:hi> turned to <ns0:hi>Iehojakim,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 23.34. and by him set up, he reigned wickedly, and infinitely oppressed the people for mony, for <ns0:hi>Pharaoh Necho</ns0:hi> that made him King verse 35. he reigned but eleven years, but rebelling against <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi> King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> as we read, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.1, 2. he was carried by him into <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> in fetters, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.6. where for ought we read he dyed. <ns0:hi>Iehojachin</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ieconi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ah</ns0:hi> his Son succeeded him, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 9. reigning only three months, and ten dayes.</ns0:note>. They shall not lament for him, <ns0:hi>saying,</ns0:hi> Ah my brother, or ah sister: they shall not lament for him, <ns0:hi>saying,</ns0:hi> Ah Lord! or ah his glory <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He died not lamented, for as it is not proba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble his Enemies would lament him, so he had disobliged his own people by violence and oppression to that degree, that it is not likely that those of them that were in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> made any great lamentation for him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 36.30.</ns0:note> He shall be buried with the burial of an ass <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">That is he shall not be buried at all, or he shall be buri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in an indecent and contemptible manner, none attending him to his Grave, none mourning for him.</ns0:note>, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The last words of this verse incline some to think that <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> was buried near to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> but the Scripture, which mentioneth his be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing carried into <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> saith nothing of his being brought back, nor is that very probable which some say, that the King of <ns0:hi>Ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bylon</ns0:hi> thought to have carried him to <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> but upon second thoughts altered his purposes, and caused him to be <ns0:hi>slain</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem,</ns0:hi> and his body to be ignominiously dragged out of the gates. The Scripture saith expresly he was carried to <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.15. and if he died there, yet this Text remaineth true, the scope of which seemeth to be to shew the vanity of this Prince in his great and stately Buildings, which he was not like long to enjoy, nor to be buried nigh to them, nor in any degree of honour proportionate to the splendor of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Go up to Lebanon <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The Hebrew Verb being feminine lets us know, that <ns0:hi>Ierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem</ns0:hi> was the place to which this speech is directed. To the in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />habitants of which the Prophet here calleth, to whom he calleth to go up to <ns0:hi>Lebanon.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and cry, and lift up thy voice in Bashan <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">And to <ns0:hi>Bashan,</ns0:hi> both <ns0:hi>Lebanon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Basan</ns0:hi> were<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Hills or Places that looked towards <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> from whence the Jews looked for help, and had it sometimes, as 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 16.7. he calls to them ironically to go up to the mountainous parts of them, where standing and crying, they might be soonest and best heard.</ns0:note>, and cry from the pas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sages <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">What we Translate <ns0:hi>from the passages,</ns0:hi> others translate <ns0:hi>from the borders,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>from the sides.</ns0:hi> Others from <ns0:hi>Abarim</ns0:hi> which is the name of a mountain, as well as <ns0:hi>Lebanon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Basan,</ns0:hi> vide <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 27.12. and 33.47. which seemeth to me the best interpretation, the meaning is, go and cry, for help from all places but it will be in vain, for</ns0:note>: for all thy lovers are destroyed <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">the <ns0:hi>Egyptians</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Assyri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans</ns0:hi> to whom thou were wont heretofore to fly, chusing rather to trust in them then in me, are themselves in the power or dan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger of the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans,</ns0:hi> who shall also destroy thee.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 I spake to thee in thy <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>prosperi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> prosperity <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">I, by my Prophets, spake to thee while all things went well with thee, so as thou hast not sinned ignorantly or without warning, I have not surprized thee with my judgments, but thou refusedst to hearken, and obey my admonitions, and pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepts.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> thou saidst I will not hear <ns0:hi>s:</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 7.23. &c.</ns0:note> this <ns0:hi>hath been</ns0:hi> thy manner from thy youth, that thou obeyedst not my voice <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">From the time that I brought thee out of the land of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> thou hast been thus a rebellious people.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 The wind shall eat up all thy pastours <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Either a vain hope, and presumption shall destroy thy Rulers and Governours, who flatter thee with promises of pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sperity, or a judgment shall sieze them, that shall be like a vi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />olent Wind, which presently scattereth the Clouds, and the smoak, or they shall be blasted by my judgments, as Plants are blasted; and eaten up by Winds.</ns0:note>, and thy lovers shall go into captivity <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And those that have been thy Friends, and Allies, <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> in whom thou hast trusted, shall themselves be made captive<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note>, surely then shalt thou be ashamed, and confounded for all thy wickedness <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Surely when thou seest this, thou wilt be convinced, and ashamed of thy wicked courses.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 O <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>inhabit<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ress.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> inhabitant of Lebanon <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> which is called an inhabitant of <ns0:hi>Lebanon,</ns0:hi> either because their Houses were built of Wood cut down out of the Forrest of <ns0:hi>Lebanon,</ns0:hi> or because they lived in as great plenty, and delight, as if they lived in <ns0:hi>Lebanon</ns0:hi>; Or because they thought the mountain of <ns0:hi>Lebanon</ns0:hi> was a certain refuge to them.</ns0:note> that makest thy nest in the cedars <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">They are said to <ns0:hi>make their nest in the Cedars</ns0:hi>; either because their houses were built of the <ns0:hi>Cedars of Lebanon,</ns0:hi> or because of the se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />curity they promised themselves, from that Forest and Moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain so full of, and famous for <ns0:hi>Cedars.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, how gracious shalt thou be <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">What favour wilt thou find</ns0:note> when pangs come upon thee, the pain as of a woman in travail <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">when my judgments shall come upon thee, as suddenly and as smartly, as the pains of a woman in travel come upon her, a simi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litude often made use of by this Prophet, to express the sudden<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, unavoidableness and greatness of Judgments, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 4.31. and 6.24. and 13.21. and 30.6. and 49.24, and 50.43. and so in other Scriptures, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 48.6. <ns0:hi>Micah<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 4.9. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salonians</ns0:hi> 5.3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">
                  <ns0:hi>As</ns0:hi> I live saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehojakim king of Judah <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>Coniah</ns0:hi> he meaneth <ns0:hi>Iehojachin,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.8. whose name was <ns0:hi>Iecohiah,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.16. (for all <ns0:hi>Iosiahs</ns0:hi> Sons had two names and so had his Granchild <ns0:hi>Ieconiah</ns0:hi>) here in contempt called <ns0:hi>Coniah.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> were the signet upon my right hand <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He saith that though this <ns0:hi>Coniah</ns0:hi> were as dear to him as his signet, which every man keepeth safe, yet this should not secure him from divine vengeance.</ns0:note>, yet would I pluck thee thence.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And I will give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">That is into the power of the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Babylonians,</ns0:hi> whom they were fraid of, and justly, for they thirsted after their blood, and ruine.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>of them</ns0:hi> whose face thou fear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est, even into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deans.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And I will cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another countrey where ye were not born, and there ye shall dye <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Ieconiahs</ns0:hi> Mother was <ns0:hi>Nehushtan,</ns0:hi> the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Elma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.8. verse 12. the fulfilling of this Prophesie is recorded, it is said, that <ns0:hi>Iehojachin the King of Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah went out to the King of Babylon, he and his Mother, and his Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants,</ns0:hi> &c. so <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 15. together with eight thousand prisoners of the meaner sort, besides Princes and Nobles.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">But to the land whereunto they <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>lift up their mind.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> desire to return, thither they shall not return <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">That is they shall never come again to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> though they be fond of it as their Native Countrey, and may promise themselves such favours from the <ns0:hi>King of Babylon,</ns0:hi> yet there shall no such thing be their portion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 <ns0:hi>Is</ns0:hi> this man Coniah a despised broken idol <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Prophet either speaketh this in the person of God, or of the people, who are here brought in, affirming that this Prince who was the idol of the people, was now through the just judgment of God become like a broken idol.</ns0:note>? <ns0:hi>is he</ns0:hi> a vessel wherein <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> no pleasure <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Or like a vessel which men care not for, being either so crackt, or so tainted, that they can make no use of it, and admiring at this <ns0:hi>Catastrophe,</ns0:hi> and inquiring the cause why it so came to pass.</ns0:note>? wherefore are they cast out, he and his seed <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He, and <ns0:hi>his seed,</ns0:hi> it is said <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 30. that no man of his seed should prosper sitting upon the <ns0:hi>throne of David, and ruling any more in Iudah,</ns0:hi> nor is there any mention made of any of his Children where his carrying into Captivity is recorded, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.12. which makes some think that by <ns0:hi>his seed</ns0:hi> here is meant the poste<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity of his Grand Father <ns0:hi>Iosiah,</ns0:hi> but others think, that he had <ns0:hi>Children,</ns0:hi> either before he went into the captivity, or born while he was in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.12. it is said that <ns0:hi>after they were b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ought to Babylon, Ieconiah begat Salathiel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and are cast into a land which they know not?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">By Earth he either means the Land of <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> to which he calls thrice, to signifie the deafness of this people, and unwil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lingness to hear, and believe what God spake by him. Or else he calls to the whole Earth, as he calls <ns0:hi>Heaven</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Earth</ns0:hi> to wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, <ns0:hi>Deuteronomy</ns0:hi> 30.19. and 32.1. <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 1.2. and 34.1. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 6.19.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:32" />30 Thus saith the LORD, Write ye this man childless <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The word translated <ns0:hi>Childless,</ns0:hi> is but thrice read in Holy Writ, and by various interpreters translated, <ns0:hi>barren,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>increa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing, empty, full of sorrow, wanting Children,</ns0:hi> &c. it is thought to be interpreted, by the next words, <ns0:hi>no man of his seed shall prosper sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Iudah,</ns0:hi> for there are seven of his Sons named 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 3.17. So that he is said to be <ns0:hi>Childless,</ns0:hi> either because all his Children dyed be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore their Father. Or (which is most probable,) because he had no Child that sate upon the Throne, or ever had any Rulers place in <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> but onely some that lived in a mean condition in Captivity, amongst whom <ns0:hi>Salathiel</ns0:hi> is named, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.12. as a Progenitor of Christ.</ns0:note>, a man <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> shall not prosper in his dayes: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah.</ns0:p>
